accepted_examples.german: Habt ihr den Unfall mit eigenen Augen gesehen?
accepted_examples.english: Did you see the accident with your own eyes?
accepted_examples.note: Auge is used in the plural Augen, in the visual organ sense.

accepted_examples.german: Du bist noch zu jung, um zu sterben.
accepted_examples.note: sterben means to die in the infinitive construction.

accepted_examples.german: Tom und Maria bauen draußen einen Schneemann.
accepted_examples.english: Tom and Mary are outside building a snowman.
accepted_examples.note: draußen means outside, in the open air.
runter is directional and matches down here.

accepted_examples.german: An der Kirche gehe ich jeden Tag vorbei.
accepted_examples.english: I walk past that church every day.
accepted_examples.note: vorbei means past in this movement construction.

accepted_examples.english: Leave me alone and let me do my job.
accepted_examples.note: arbeiten means to work/do one's job.

accepted_examples.german: Schließ die Tür hinter dir, wenn du gehst!
accepted_examples.english: Shut the door behind you when you leave.
accepted_examples.note: hinter expresses the spatial relation behind.

accepted_examples.german: Tom ist mein einzig wirklicher Freund.
accepted_examples.english: Tom is my only real friend.

accepted_examples.german: Er hat eine Tochter, die sehr hübsch ist.
accepted_examples.english: He has a daughter who is very pretty.

accepted_examples.german: Tom hat eine Schwester, die gerne Tennis spielt.
accepted_examples.english: Tom has a sister who likes to play tennis.

accepted_examples.german: Ich will sehen, was da drin ist.
accepted_examples.english: I want to see what's inside.

accepted_examples.note: ruhig is used adverbially to describe how Tom sat.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist nicht zu spät, das zu tun.
accepted_examples.english: It's not too late to do that.

accepted_examples.german: Der Kerl sieht genau so aus wie Tom.
accepted_examples.english: That guy looks exactly like Tom.
accepted_examples.note: Kerl means guy/fellow in this colloquial sentence.

accepted_examples.german: Müssen wir flach auf dem Boden liegen?
accepted_examples.english: Do we have to lie flat on the ground?
accepted_examples.note: liegen means to be in a horizontal position.

accepted_examples.german: Er ist so arm wie eh und je.
accepted_examples.english: He is as poor as ever.
accepted_examples.note: je means ever in the idiom eh und je.

accepted_examples.german: Es ist noch keiner dieser Äpfel reif.
accepted_examples.english: None of these apples are ripe yet.
accepted_examples.note: keiner means none; the sentence concerns none of the apples.

accepted_examples.german: Der Teufel hat mich dazu gezwungen.
accepted_examples.english: The devil made me do it.

held_examples.german: Lass es dort, wo du es gefunden hast.
held_examples.reason: This is a perfect-tense verb use of finden, not an adjectival use of gefunden.

held_examples.german: Hier halten Pärchen gewöhnlich nicht in aller Öffentlichkeit Händchen.
held_examples.reason: This is the idiom Händchen halten; it does not illustrate the listed sense of holding an object.

held_examples.german: Lassen Sie uns später darauf zurück kommen.
held_examples.reason: darauf zurückkommen means return to a topic; it does not illustrate the listed following/after sense.

held_examples.german: Die Gräten sind doch kein Grund, nicht gerne Fisch zu essen!
held_examples.reason: The entry's word class and gloss were wrong, and the supplied English pair is awkward; use a new example for the corrected adverb sense.

held_examples.german: Die Brücke wird gerade neu gestrichen.
held_examples.reason: neu means anew/again here, not new as a property of a noun.

held_examples.german: Maria ist sogar noch schöner als Elke.
held_examples.reason: The supplied English translation changes both personal names; use a corrected editorial example.

held_examples.german: Er weiß gar nicht, was er verloren hat.
held_examples.reason: This is a verbal perfect-tense use of verlieren, not the adjectival lost/missing sense.

editorial_examples.german: Der gefundene Schlüssel lag unter dem Tisch.
editorial_examples.english: The key we found was under the table.
editorial_examples.note: Adjectivally used Partizip II gefundene modifies Schlüssel; it matches the entry's found/located sense.

editorial_examples.german: Bitte halten Sie das Glas mit beiden Händen.
editorial_examples.english: Please hold the glass with both hands.
editorial_examples.note: This illustrates halten with a physical object.
darauf expresses that the event followed shortly after.
Corrected the entry to the adverb gerne, gladly/with pleasure.

editorial_examples.german: Sie hat sich ein neues Fahrrad gekauft.
editorial_examples.note: neu describes a recently acquired item.

editorial_examples.german: Sogar Tom konnte die Tür nicht öffnen.
editorial_examples.english: Even Tom couldn't open the door.
editorial_examples.note: sogar adds an unexpected or emphatic case.

editorial_examples.german: Der verlorene Schlüssel lag unter dem Sofa.
editorial_examples.english: The lost key was under the sofa.
editorial_examples.note: verloren is used adjectivally to mean lost/missing.

entry_updates.note: Duden classifies gern/gerne as an adverb meaning with willing pleasure; the prior entry gloss incorrectly described a reply to thanks.

usage_notes.value: Stifter is also recorded as a rare plural; Stifte is the usual learner form.
usage_notes.note: Duden marks Stifter as a rare plural for the ecclesiastical institution sense.

usage_notes.value: Kerls is a North German colloquial variant; Kerle is the usual learner form.
usage_notes.note: Duden marks Kerls as North German colloquial.

plural_reviews.note: For the adult-male sense, use Männer; remove Mann, which is a number expression, not the regular plural for this sense.
For female parent, the plural is Mütter; other meanings have other plurals.
For a political country/state, the plural is Länder; Lande is archaic/poetic and belongs to other usages.
For individual lexical units, use Wörter; Worte refers to utterances or connected meaning.
The standard plural for the person/title sense is Doktoren; omit Latin doctores/Doktores from the learner plural.
The plural is Abstände; preserve the umlaut spelling.
For the endowed ecclesiastical institution/monastery sense, Stifte is the ordinary plural; Stifter is rare.
Both Dilemmas and Dilemmata are accepted plural forms.
Both forms are recorded by Duden; plural use is rare.
Kerle is the usual plural for guy/fellow; Kerls is a North German colloquial variant.
